scope: Reusable teaching-context and usage references. A source below does not attest every translation in common-core.json. Per-entry evidence links state their limited scope; unlinked forms remain editorial candidates.

sources.title: Japan Foundation Irodori Starter — lesson 1
sources.supports: Beginner greetings, polite/familiar thanks, apology and context-dependent farewells. Includes こんにちは, おはようございます, こんばんは, ありがとうございます, すみません, おやすみなさい, じゃあ、また.
sources.limits: Situational A1 examples, not a universal frequency ranking or certification of other languages.

sources.title: Japan Foundation Irodori Starter — lesson 2
sources.supports: Communication repair for beginners: もういちど、お願いします and もう少し、ゆっくり言ってください; not understanding and asking someone to repeat.
sources.limits: Exact wording in an entry may be a shorter editorial adaptation, which must be labelled.

sources.title: A Native’s Guide to the Latvian Language — Latvia.eu
sources.supports: Latvian greeting/register distinctions; Labdien, Labrīt, Labvakar, Uz redzēšanos, Paldies, Lūdzu, Atvainojiet, Prieks iepazīties. Explains familiar versus stranger-facing forms.
sources.limits: Practical introductory guide, not a corpus or a dictionary for all proposed expressions.

sources.title: Gramota — пожалуйста
sources.supports: Russian пожалуйста as polite request/agreement expression; use depends on speech act.
sources.limits: Does not validate all Russian phrase translations. Other Russian audit dictionary evidence is linked per finding.

sources.title: Cambridge English Grammar Today — Requests
sources.supports: Practical polite requests using can/could/may and please; urgent needs such as I need a doctor. Distinguishes direct demands from polite requests.
sources.limits: English grammar/usage framework, not a comparative frequency list or proof of LV/RU/JA equivalents.

sources.title: Oxford 3000 and 5000 learner wordlists
sources.supports: Learner usefulness and frequency are relevant selection criteria; useful vocabulary depends on meaning and context.
sources.limits: No claim that all library entries were individually matched to this list or ranked by corpus frequency.
